title: Engraving
look: A copperplate engraving: tone built from fine parallel and crossed lines, dark sepia on cream, in an oval cartouche.

doc.essence: An illustration cut into a copper plate with a burin and printed in dark ink: no flat tone at all, only lines, closer together where it is darker and crossed where it is darkest.
doc.notIt: Not pencil (crisp printed lines of even ink, crossed for dark tones, an engraved frame), not manga (lines, not dots), not woodblock (no colour, no wood grain).
doc.shapes: A thin, firm contour. Every area is ruled with parallel lines whose angle changes from part to part, so the parts read as separate planes.
doc.colour: Only dark sepia ink on cream. The gap between lines follows how dark the area was; below mid-grey a second set of lines crosses the first.
doc.eyes: Solid ink, or cream on a dark visor.
pitfalls: Close line gaps alias into moiré at small sizes: the gap never drops below 2 px.
Light palettes leave areas blank: the contour carries them.
